SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349


PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
INTERVENOR AARON EDWARD HOWTON'S RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS' OBJECTIONS TO, AND MOTION TO STRIKE, INTERVENOR TESTIMONY
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
Intervenor Aaron Edward Howton files this Response to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation's Objections to, and Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony. Mr. Howton respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges deny the motion to strike his Direct Testimony, or alternatively reserve ruling until the hearing so that he may sponsor his testimony under oath, be subject to voir dire if requested, and submit to cross-examination.
I. SUMMARY OF RESPONSE
Applicants appear to seek to strike or limit portions of intervenor testimony on hearsay and qualification grounds. As applied to Mr. Howton, that objection should be denied. Mr. Howton's Direct Testimony is not an out-of-court statement being offered through some other witness; it is his own prefiled direct testimony in this contested case. He is prepared to appear in person, swear that the testimony is true and accurate, and be cross-examined. Under SOAH and PUC procedure, written direct testimony may be admitted into evidence after the witness is sworn and identifies the testimony as the testimony he would give orally.
Mr. Howton also has specialized education, training, and experience directly related to the matters addressed in his testimony, including wildlife science, ornithology, herpetology, mammalogy, entomology, federal wildlife and agricultural enforcement, emergency services, law enforcement, wildlife game warden programs, Endangered Species Act compliance, and current agricultural and wildlife-management operations on his farm. Applicants may challenge the weight to be given to that testimony through cross-examination, but the testimony should not be stricken in advance.
II. ARGUMENT
A. Prefiled Direct Testimony Is Proper Evidence When Sponsored by the Witness.
SOAH Rule 155.429 expressly allows direct testimony to be filed in writing before the hearing in narrative or question-and-answer form. Once the witness is sworn and identifies the written testimony as a true record of what the witness would have testified to orally, the written testimony may be admitted into evidence as if read or presented orally. See 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 155.429(c)(1)(A)-(D).
The PUC's rule governing written testimony is consistent with that procedure. Written testimony may be received as an exhibit and incorporated into the record without being read aloud, provided the witness is sworn, confirms that the testimony is true and accurate, and submits to cross-examination, clarifying questions, redirect examination, and recross-examination. See 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 22.225(b).
For that reason, Mr. Howton's filed Direct Testimony should not be characterized as inadmissible hearsay merely because it was filed before the hearing. It is the method ordered and permitted for presenting direct testimony in this case. Mr. Howton will sponsor the testimony under oath and will be available for cross-examination.
B. Mr. Howton Is Qualified by Knowledge, Skill, Experience, Training, and Education.
Texas Rule of Evidence 702 permits testimony from a witness qualified by knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education if the testimony will assist the trier of fact in understanding the evidence or determining a fact issue. Mr. Howton is not offering unsupported rumor. He is offering opinions and observations based on approximately sixty years of specialized education, professional training, federal service, enforcement experience, and land and wildlife-management experience.
Mr. Howton graduated from Texas A&M University in 1970 with a Bachelor of Science degree in Wildlife Science. His coursework included Ornithology, Herpetology, Mammalogy, and Entomology. From 1970 to 1974, he served in the United States Air Force as an Engineering Entomologist responsible for identification and control of flora and fauna on military installations. From 1974 to 1978, he worked for the United States Department of Agriculture, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, identifying plants and animals entering the United States and taking appropriate action under USDA laws and regulations.
From 1978 to 1982, Mr. Howton served with the USDA Office of Inspector General as a Special Agent Criminal Investigator conducting investigations involving federal laws. From 1982 to 2009, he was employed by the United States Department of the Army as Deputy Director of Emergency Services, with responsibilities involving law enforcement programs, Wildlife Game Wardens, Military Police, Physical Security, Fire Department Operations, Anti-Terrorism, and enforcement of laws and Army regulations, including the Endangered Species Act and other federal statutes protecting wildlife. Since 2009, he has conducted farming and agricultural operations and wildlife management on a farm registered with the USDA Farm Service Agency.
This background is sufficient, at minimum, to allow Mr. Howton to provide lay factual testimony based on personal knowledge and to provide specialized opinions within the scope of his education, training, and experience. Any disagreement by Applicants goes to weight, not wholesale admissibility.
C. The Testimony Is Based on Personal Knowledge and Specialized Experience, Not Mere Hearsay.
To the extent Mr. Howton testifies about his own property, agricultural operations, wildlife-management practices, observations, education, employment history, and experience with federal wildlife and agricultural laws, that testimony is based on personal knowledge. Such testimony is not hearsay.
To the extent Mr. Howton relies on technical, scientific, regulatory, or agency materials, such materials may be considered as part of the basis for his opinions and may also be addressed through exhibits, official notice, cross-examination, or argument concerning weight. A blanket hearsay objection should not be used to strike an intervenor's entire testimony where the witness is available to sponsor the testimony and explain the basis for his opinions.
D. Striking the Testimony Would Be Unfairly Prejudicial and Inconsistent With the Development of a Complete Record.
This proceeding concerns a 765-kV transmission line that may materially affect private property, agricultural operations, wildlife habitat, and landowners' use and enjoyment of their land. Mr. Howton is an affected landowner and intervenor. His testimony provides relevant facts, observations, and specialized opinions for the Administrative Law Judges and the Commission to consider in evaluating routing issues.
If Applicants believe any particular sentence exceeds the proper scope of Mr. Howton's expertise, the appropriate remedy is not to strike the testimony in its entirety. The Administrative Law Judges may receive the testimony subject to cross-examination, limit or assign weight to particular opinions, or permit voir dire where appropriate. Mr. Howton expressly agrees to appear, be sworn, authenticate his testimony, and answer cross-examination.
III. PRAYER
For the reasons stated above, Intervenor Aaron Edward Howton respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges deny Applicants' motion to strike his Direct Testimony and overrule the hearsay objection as applied to his testimony. In the alternative, Mr. Howton requests that the Administrative Law Judges reserve ruling until the hearing, allow voir dire if requested, allow him to sponsor his testimony under oath, and admit his testimony subject to cross-examination and the Administrative Law Judges' determination of the appropriate weight to be given to the testimony.
Mr. Howton further requests all other relief, at law or in equity, to which he may be justly entitled.
Respectfully submitted,
